claim: Ticagrelor is a first-line drug for the treatment of acute ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
source: Ticagrelor is a first-line drug for the treatment of acute ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to clinical guidelines in the introduction section.

claim: Approximately 20% STEMI patients taking ticagrelor exhibited a delayed response.
source: However, approximately 20% STEMI patients taking ticagrelor exhibited a delayed response and the mechanism was still unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background information, likely based on prior research.

claim: The plasma concentrations of ticagrelor and AR-C124910XX were lower in HPR patients than controls.
source: Pharmacokinetic assessment result showed that the plasma concentrations of ticagrelor and its metabolism production, AR-C124910XX, were lower in HPR patients than controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements presented in the study.

claim: There is no difference in ABCB1 gene expression between the NPR group and the HPR group.
source: Further single nucloetide polymorphism (SNP) analysis identified that there is no difference in ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1 (ABCB1) gene expression between the NPR group and the HPR group.
evidence: This is based on SNP analysis data presented in the study.

claim: HPR patients had higher microbial richness and diversity.
source: Metagenomic and metabolomic analyses of fecal samples showed that HPR patients had higher microbial richness and diversity.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data presented in the study.

claim: Transplantation of the gut microbiota from HPR donors to microbiota-depleted mice decreased plasma concentration of ticagrelor.
source: Transplantation of the gut microbiota from HPR donors to microbiota-depleted mice obviously decreased plasma concentration of ticagrelor.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from fecal microbiota transplantation experiments.

claim: Gut microbiota dysbiosis may be an important mechanism for ticagrelor HPR in patients with STEMI.
source: Our findings highlight that gut microbiota dysbiosis may be an important mechanism for the ticagrelor of HPR in patients with STEMI and support that modify gut microbiota is a potential therapeutic option for STEMI.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and analyses presented in the study.

claim: Clopidogrel and prasugrel require metabolic activation and irreversibly bind to the P2Y12 receptor.
source: Moreover, clopidogrel and prasugrel require metabolic activation and irreversibly bind to the P2Y12 receptor, causing prolonged recovery of platelet function.
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge about these drugs.

claim: Ticagrelor does not require metabolic activation and binds rapidly and reversibly to the P2Y12 receptor.
source: In contrast to clopidogrel and prasugrel, ticagrelor does not require metabolic activation and binds rapidly and reversibly to the P2Y12 receptor.
evidence: This is established pharmacological knowledge about ticagrelor.

claim: Ticagrelor undergoes cytochrome P450 (CYP)-mediated metabolism to produce the active metabolite AR-C124910XX.
source: However, it undergoes cytochrome P450 (CYP)-mediated metabolism to produce the active metabolite AR-C124910XX (Yandrapalli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: AR-C124910XX has approximately 30% activation of the parent drug to exhibit antiplatelet activity.
source: AR-C124910XX, the main known active metabolite, has approximately 30% activation of the parent drug to exhibit antiplatelet activity (Mehta et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The latest American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association guidelines recommend ticagrelor as a first-line drug for the treatment of acute STEMI.
source: As it quickly and strongly came into effect compared to the conventional drug clopidogrel, the latest American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association guidelines recommend ticagrelor as a first-line drug for the treatment of acute STEMI (Levine et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to clinical guidelines.

claim: Some STEMI patients respond poorly to ticagrelor, exhibiting a delayed response in the early phase of treatment even when a loading dose of 180 mg was employed.
source: However, some STEMI patients respond poorly to ticagrelor, exhibiting a delayed response in the early phase of treatment even when a loading dose of 180 mg was employed.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from clinical practice, likely supported by prior studies.

claim: There is a crucial time window after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) that cannot be protected by ticagrelor, in which some STEMI patients are at a high risk of stent thrombosis.
source: There is a crucial time window after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) that cannot be protected by ticagrelor, in which some STEMI patients are at a high risk of stent thrombosis (Alexopoulos et al., 2012; Bagai et al., 2018; Franchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Genetic and non-genetic factors have been reported to contribute to HPR in ticagrelor.
source: Genetic and non-genetic factors have been reported to contribute to its HPR (Siller-Matula et al., 2016; Barbieri et al., 2016; Verdoia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Ticagrelor requires absorption in the intestine combined with the P2Y12 receptor of platelets without metabolic activation in the liver.
source: Ticagrelor requires absorption in the intestine combined with the P2Y12 receptor of platelets without metabolic activation in the liver (Weeks et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: P-glycoprotein is encoded by ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1 (ABCB1) gene.
source: P-glycoprotein is encoded by ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1 (ABCB1) gene.
evidence: This is established molecular biology knowledge.

claim: P-glycoprotein affects the absorption and metabolism of ticagrelor in the intestine.
source: As an important transporter, it affects the absorption and metabolism of ticagrelor in the intestine (Varenhorst et al., 2015; Notarangelo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: P-glycoprotein mostly exists in the apical membrane of the intestinal mucosa, liver, and kidney.
source: P-glycoprotein, also known as ABCB1 protein, is one of the adenosine triphosphate binding cassette genes that mostly exist in the apical membrane of the intestinal mucosa, liver, and kidney (von Richter et al., 2004; Fromm and Kim, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Valspodar has a significant inhibitory effect on the efflux of ticagrelor, suggesting that P-glycoprotein is involved in the oral disposal of ticagrelor.
source: Marsousi et al., 2016, revealed a significant inhibitory effect of the P-glycoprotein inhibitor valspodar on the efflux of ticagrelor, suggesting that P-glycoprotein is involved in the oral disposal of ticagrelor.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: A large genetic substudy of the PLATO trial showed that CYP2C19 and ABCB1 polymorphisms were independent of the lower rates of cardiovascular death, MI, or stroke observed in patients treated with ticagrelor.
source: A large genetic substudy of the PLATO trial showed that CYP2C19 and ABCB1 polymorphisms were independent of the lower rates of cardiovascular death, MI, or stroke observed in patients treated with ticagrelor (Varenhorst et al., 2015; Nardin et al., 2018; Wallentin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A genome-wide association study of patients from the PLATO study identified a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) associated with the solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 (SLCO1B1) gene that leads to decreased organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B1 (OATP1B1) activity.
source: In addition, a genome-wide association study of patients from the PLATO study identified a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) associated with the solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 (SLCO1B1) gene that leads to decreased organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B1 (OATP1B1) activity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research (implied from context).

claim: Plasma ticagrelor levels were associated with two independent SNPs in the CYP3A4 region and an SNP in the UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B7 (UGT2B7) gene.
source: Plasma ticagrelor levels were associated with two independent SNPs in the CYP3A4 region and an SNP in the UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B7 (UGT2B7) gene (Varenhorst et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Alterations of the gut microbiome and its products may affect the progress and state of cardiovascular disease.
source: There is growing awareness that alterations of the gut microbiome and its products may affect the progress and state of cardiovascular disease (Zhernakova et al., 2018; Jie et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The association between gut microbiota and ticagrelor has not been reported previously.
source: The association between gut microbiota and ticagrelor has not been reported previously, and the specific components of microbiota that influence the effect of drugs leading to the occurrence of HPR remain unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature.

claim: All patients with STEMI were enrolled in the Department of Cardiology of the General Hospital of Shenyang Military Region between April 2016 and March 2018.
source: All patients with STEMI were enrolled in the Department of Cardiology of the General Hospital of Shenyang Military Region between April 2016 and March 2018.
evidence: This describes the study cohort and enrollment period.

claim: All patients received ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose followed by two 90 mg maintenance doses) and aspirin (300 mg loading dose followed by a 100 mg maintenance dose) before PCI.
source: All patients (the onset time for STEMI is ≤12 hr) received ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose followed by two 90 mg maintenance doses) and aspirin (300 mg loading dose followed by a 100 mg maintenance dose) before PCI.
evidence: This describes the treatment protocol used in the study.

claim: STEMI patients were clinically diagnosed using a combination of acute ischemic-type chest pain in the last 24 hr, electrocardiogram change, and elevated plasma hscTnT.
source: Briefly, STEMI patients were clinically diagnosed using a combination of the following criteria: (1) acute ischemic-type chest pain in the last 24 hr; (2) electrocardiogram change (pathological Q wave, ST segment elevation, or depression); (3) elevated plasma hscTnT (0.05 ng/mL) (Ibanez et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the diagnostic criteria used in the study, supported by citation.

claim: According to the rate of PA at 2 hr, patients were divided into two groups: HPR group (PA ≥59%) and NPR group (PA <59%).
source: According to the rate of PA at 2 hr, patients were divided into two groups: HPR group (PA ≥59%) and normal platelet reactivity (NPR) group (PA <59%).
evidence: This describes the classification criteria used in the study.

claim: There was no significant difference in sex composition, age, weight, and past medical history between the NPR and HPR groups.
source: There was no significant difference in sex composition, age, weight, and past medical history between the two groups (p > 0.05, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of baseline characteristics.

claim: Before taking ticagrelor (0 hr), there was no significant difference between NPR group and HPR group (p = 0.118).
source: Before taking ticagrelor (0 hr), there was no significant difference between NPR group and HPR group (p = 0.118).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of baseline platelet aggregation.

claim: The PA of NPR group and HPR group were 66.0% ± 23.5% and 73.4% ± 20.4%, respectively, before taking ticagrelor.
source: The PA of NPR group and HPR group were 66.0% ± 23.5% and 73.4% ± 20.4%, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by measurement data.

claim: After ticagrelor administration, the PA at each time point was lower than that at 0 hr (p < 0.05).
source: After ticagrelor administrated, the PA at each time point was lower than that at 0 hr (p < 0.05).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of platelet aggregation measurements over time.

claim: The PA of patients in the HPR group was higher than that in NPR group at 2, 4, 6, and 8 hr (the p-value at each time point <0.001).
source: And the PA of patients in the HPR group was higher than that in NPR group at 2, 4, 6, and 8 hr (the p-value at each time point <0.001) (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis and shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The decreasing range of PA in the HPR group was lower than that in the NPR group, and did not show the lowest value within 24 hr in the HPR group.
source: The decreasing range of PA in the HPR group was lower than that in the NPR group, and did not show the lowest value within 24 hr in the HPR group.
evidence: This is an observation from the platelet aggregation data.

claim: In the NPR group, the PA decreased the most at 2 hr after ticagrelor administration, and the lowest value (27.72 ± 16.17) of PA was detected at 4 hr after medication administration.
source: In the NPR group, the PA decreased the most at 2 hr after ticagrelor administration, and the lowest value (27.72 ± 16.17) of PA was detected at 4 hr after medication administration.
evidence: This is supported by measurement data.

claim: Within 24 hr after the administration of 180 mg ticagrelor, the blood concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group was significantly lower than that in the NPR group, especially during 2, 4, and 6 hr (all p < 0.0001).
source: Within 24 hr after the administration of 180 mg ticagrelor, the blood concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group was significantly lower than that in the NPR group, especially during 2, 4, and 6 hr (all p < 0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements and statistical analysis.

claim: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor increased rapidly in the NPR group after administration of the loading dose, and reached its peak at 4 hr.
source: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor increased rapidly in the NPR group after administration of the loading dose, and reached its peak at 4 hr.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements.

claim: The maximal plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the NPR group was 478.1 ± 430.4 ng/mL.
source: The maximal plasma concentration of ticagrelor was 478.1 ± 430.4 ng/mL.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements.

claim: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group increased gradually within 24 hr and reached its maximum (233.7 ± 195.1 ng/mL) at 24 hr.
source: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group increased gradually within 24 hr and reached its maximum (233.7 ± 195.1 ng/mL) at 24 hr (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The plasma concentration of AR-C124910XX at 2, 4, 6, and 8 hr in the HPR group was significantly lower than that in the NPR group (all p < 0.05).
source: The plasma concentration of AR-C124910XX at 2, 4, 6, and 8 hr in the HPR group was significantly lower than that in the NPR group (all p < 0.05) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements and statistical analysis, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The pharmacokinetic abnormality of ticagrelor mainly occurs in the absorption stage of the drug.
source: This suggests that the pharmacokinetic abnormality of ticagrelor mainly occurs in the absorption stage of the drug.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pharmacokinetic data showing reduced plasma concentrations.

claim: There was no significant difference in allele frequency or genotype distribution among the three SNPs of ABCB1 between the HPR and NPR groups.
source: There was no significant difference in allele frequency or genotype distribution among the three SNPs of ABCB1 between the two groups, which suggests that the high reactivity of ticagrelor is not affected by the polymorphic drug transporter ABCB1.
evidence: This is supported by genotyping data and statistical analysis presented in Table 1.

claim: The high reactivity of ticagrelor is not affected by the polymorphic drug transporter ABCB1.
source: There was no significant difference in allele frequency or genotype distribution among the three SNPs of ABCB1 between the two groups, which suggests that the high reactivity of ticagrelor is not affected by the polymorphic drug transporter ABCB1.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genotyping data.

claim: α-Diversity indices (chao1, observed species diversity index, PD whole tree, and good coverage diversity index) were significantly higher in the HPR group than in NPR group (p < 0.05).
source: α-Diversity is the analysis of species diversity in a single sample, including chao1 (Figure 2A), observed species diversity index (Figure 2B), PD whole tree (Figure 2C), and good coverage diversity index (Figure 2D). These were significantly higher in the HPR group than in NPR group (p < 0.05), which demonstrated increased species richness in the HPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data and shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: The HPR group demonstrated increased species richness compared to the NPR group.
source: These were significantly higher in the HPR group than in NPR group (p < 0.05), which demonstrated increased species richness in the HPR group.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the α-diversity analysis.

claim: Significant differences were found in β-diversity based on the unweighted (qualitative, ANOSIM R = 0.068, p = 0.012) but not the weighted (quantitative, ANOSIM R = –0.016, p = 0.691) UniFrac distance.
source: Significant differences were also found in β-diversity based on the unweighted (qualitative, ANOSIM R = 0.068, p = 0.012, Figure 2F) and not the weighted (quantitative, ANOSIM R = –0.016, p = 0.691, Figure 2E), indicating that the fecal microbial structure in the HPR group was significantly different from that of the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data and shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: The fecal microbial structure in the HPR group was significantly different from that of the NPR group.
source: Significant differences were also found in β-diversity based on the unweighted (qualitative, ANOSIM R = 0.068, p = 0.012, Figure 2F) and not the weighted (quantitative, ANOSIM R = –0.016, p = 0.691, Figure 2E), indicating that the fecal microbial structure in the HPR group was significantly different from that of the NPR group.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the β-diversity analysis.

claim: There were 21 species of bacteria at the genus level in all subjects, and 17 species of bacteria in the HPR group were more abundant than those in the NPR group, including Bacillus, Methylbacterium, Staphylococcus, Acinetobacter, and Brevibacterium.
source: There were 21 species of bacteria at the genus level in all subjects, and 17 species of bacteria in the HPR group were more abundant than those in the NPR group, including Bacillus, Methylbacterium, Staphylococcus, Acinetobacter, and Brevibacterium.
evidence: This is supported by LEfSe analysis of metagenomic data.

claim: Among the gut microbiota in the HPR group, the most important family/genera are Staphylococcaceae, Staphylococcus; Sphingomonadaceae, Sphingomonas; Cellulomonadaceae, Cellulomonas; and Lactobacillaceae, Lactobacillus.
source: It can be seen from the figure that among the gut microbiota in the HPR group, the most important family/genera are Staphylococcaceae, Staphylococcus; Sphingomonadaceae, Sphingomonas; Cellulomonadaceae, Cellulomonas; and Lactobacillaceae, Lactobacillus.
evidence: This is supported by LEfSe analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There were significant differences in fecal microbiota between the HPR and NPR groups.
source: These results indicated that there were significant differences in fecal microbiota between the HPR and NPR groups.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the metagenomic analysis.

claim: The genus Staphylococcus ranked first among the most important features based on mean decrease accuracy and was found to be 8.0-fold more abundant in the HPR group than the NPR group.
source: The genus Staphylococcus ranked first among the most important features based on mean decrease accuracy and was found to be 8.0-fold more abundant in the HPR group than the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by random forest analysis of metagenomic data.

claim: Lactobacillus, Methylobacterium, and Sphingomonas were among the most important genera contributing to classification accuracy.
source: Lactobacillus, Methylobacterium, and Sphingomonas were also among the most important genera contributing to classification accuracy.
evidence: This is supported by random forest analysis of metagenomic data.

claim: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.807 (95% confidence interval: 0.612–1.0, 71.4% sensitivity, 88.9% specificity).
source: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.807 (95% confidence interval: 0.612–1.0, 71.4% sensitivity, 88.9% specificity) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by random forest predictive model analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The relative abundance of the circulatory system and cardiovascular disease was significantly higher in the HPR group than the NPR group.
source: At level 1, the main metabolic pathways with significant differences between the NPR and HPR groups are shown in Figure 4A. The relative abundance of the circulatory system and cardiovascular disease was significantly higher in the HPR group than the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by PICRUST functional analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: At level 2, there were 24 metabolic pathways involved in the difference between the NPR and HPR groups.
source: At level 2, there were 24 metabolic pathways involved in the difference between the NPR and HPR groups.
evidence: This is supported by PICRUST functional analysis.

claim: The relative abundance of phenylalanine metabolism was the highest, followed by that of cofactor and vitamin metabolism.
source: The relative abundance of phenylalanine metabolism was the highest, followed by that of cofactor and vitamin metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by PICRUST functional analysis.

claim: The relative abundance of phenylalanine metabolism and cofactor and vitamin metabolism was higher in the NPR group than in the HPR group.
source: The relative abundance of the above functions was higher in the NPR group than in the HPR group (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by PICRUST functional analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The HPR group had fewer genes related to apoptosis and ether lipid metabolism than the NPR group.
source: In contrast, the HPR group had fewer genes related to apoptosis and ether lipid metabolism than the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by PICRUST functional analysis.

claim: A total of 32 chemical constituents were identified in the metabolomic analysis.
source: A total of 32 chemical constituents were identified in this study.
evidence: This is supported by 1H NMR metabolomic analysis.

claim: The content of citrate increased in the HPR group.
source: Among them, the content of citrate increased in the HPR group, and the content of valine, glutamate, and salicylate increased in the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metabolomic analysis data.

claim: The content of valine, glutamate, and salicylate increased in the NPR group.
source: Among them, the content of citrate increased in the HPR group, and the content of valine, glutamate, and salicylate increased in the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metabolomic analysis data.

claim: Lactobacillus, Barnesiella, and Cellulomonas positively correlated with citrate and glutamate levels.
source: Correlation coefficients with statistical differences are listed in Table 2, for example, Lactobacillus, Barnesiella, and Cellulomonas positively correlated with citrate and glutamate levels, while Methylobacterium, Sphingomonas, and Staphylococcus negatively correlated with salicylate.
evidence: This is supported by Pearson's correlation analysis between microbiota and metabolites.

claim: Methylobacterium, Sphingomonas, and Staphylococcus negatively correlated with salicylate.
source: Correlation coefficients with statistical differences are listed in Table 2, for example, Lactobacillus, Barnesiella, and Cellulomonas positively correlated with citrate and glutamate levels, while Methylobacterium, Sphingomonas, and Staphylococcus negatively correlated with salicylate.
evidence: This is supported by Pearson's correlation analysis between microbiota and metabolites.

claim: Antibiotics and probiotics are important factors affecting platelet reactivity in both animal models and clinical trials.
source: Previous studies have shown that antibiotics and probiotics are important factors affecting platelet reactivity in both animal models and clinical trials (Betancur et al., 2020; Budzyński et al., 2016; Capkin and Altinok, 2009; Kang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group was lower than that in the NPR group at all time points within 24 hr after ticagrelor administration in fecal microbiota transplanted mice.
source: As expected, the plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group was lower than that in the NPR group at all time points within 24 hr after ticagrelor administration, and there were significant differences between the two groups at 1, 2, and 6 hr.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements in the fecal microbiota transplantation experiment.

claim: There were significant differences in plasma ticagrelor concentration between the HPR and NPR groups at 1, 2, and 6 hr in fecal microbiota transplanted mice.
source: As expected, the plasma concentration of ticagrelor in the HPR group was lower than that in the NPR group at all time points within 24 hr after ticagrelor administration, and there were significant differences between the two groups at 1, 2, and 6 hr.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements and statistical analysis in the fecal microbiota transplantation experiment.

claim: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor in HPR increased gradually within 24 hr in fecal microbiota transplanted mice, and the overall concentration was lower than that in the NPR group.
source: The plasma concentration of ticagrelor in HPR increased gradually within 24 hr, and the overall concentration was lower than that in the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements in the fecal microbiota transplantation experiment.

claim: The overall change trend of AR-C124910XX in 24 hr was the same as that of the prototype drug in fecal microbiota transplanted mice.
source: The overall change trend of AR-C124910XX in 24 hr was the same as that of the prototype drug (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by pharmacokinetic measurements shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The change in platelet reactivity may be the mechanism by which antibiotics and probiotics regulate platelet performance.
source: Therefore, the change in platelet reactivity may be the mechanism by which antibiotics and probiotics regulate platelet performance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the fecal microbiota transplantation experiment results.

claim: Gut microbes modulated platelet reactivity after ticagrelor treatment.
source: The present study revealed an interesting finding that gut microbes modulated platelet reactivity after ticagrelor treatment.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Platelet hyperactivity plays an important role in the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases.
source: Platelet hyperactivity plays an important role in the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cardiovascular medicine.

claim: Gut microbiota are involved in the formation of many cardiac metabolic phenotypes and promote the development of atherosclerosis and other diseases.
source: In the past decade, researchers have realized that gut microbiota are involved in the formation of many cardiac metabolic phenotypes and promote the development of atherosclerosis and other diseases (Duttaroy, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Platelets of sterile mice show reduced ADP-dependent PA, indicating that the presence of symbionts sensitizes ADP-induced platelet activation.
source: It has been found that platelets of sterile mice show reduced ADP-dependent PA, indicating that the presence of symbionts sensitizes ADP-induced platelet activation (Kiouptsi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The mechanism of gut microbiota effects on platelet activation may be related to the activation of the innate immune pathway triggered by TLR2.
source: The underlying mechanism of these findings may be related to the activation of the innate immune pathway triggered by TLR2 (Jäckel et al., 2017) or activation of integrin αIIbβ3 (Kiouptsi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The mechanism of gut microbiota effects on platelet activation may be related to activation of integrin αIIbβ3.
source: The underlying mechanism of these findings may be related to the activation of the innate immune pathway triggered by TLR2 (Jäckel et al., 2017) or activation of integrin αIIbβ3 (Kiouptsi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The level of functional choline utilization C (cut C) in the gut microbiota can be transmitted through fecal transplantation, thereby enhancing platelet reactivity and thrombosis potential in the recipient.
source: Furthermore, the level of functional choline utilization C (cut C) in the gut microbiota can be transmitted through fecal transplantation, thereby enhancing platelet reactivity and thrombosis potential in the recipient (Skye et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: TMAO, an intestinal bacterial by-product, can regulate the high reactivity and clot formation rate of platelets in vivo and increase the risk of thrombosis.
source: TMAO, an intestinal bacterial by-product, can regulate the high reactivity and clot formation rate of platelets in vivo and increase the risk of thrombosis (Zhu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Intestinal microbiota is one of the determinants of pharmacokinetics that has been underestimated.
source: Intestinal microbiota is one of the determinants of pharmacokinetics that has been underestimated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: When oral drugs enter the digestive tract, they are first exposed to a large number of bacteria and active enzymes secreted by these bacteria, including oxidoreductase and transferase.
source: When oral drugs enter the digestive tract, they are first exposed to a large number of bacteria and active enzymes secreted by these bacteria, including oxidoreductase and transferase, among others.
evidence: This is established knowledge about drug metabolism.

claim: The intestinal biotransformation of drugs may occur before the first-pass effect, affecting the bioavailability and efficacy of drugs.
source: Therefore, the intestinal biotransformation of drugs may occur before the first-pass effect, affecting the bioavailability and efficacy of drugs.
evidence: This is an inference based on established pharmacological principles.

claim: The decrease in left ventricular function and intestinal blood supply caused by myocardial infarction leads to the inhibition of intestinal epithelial tight junction protein and the injury of intestinal mucosa, thereby increasing intestinal permeability.
source: Animal experiments have shown that the decrease in left ventricular function and intestinal blood supply caused by myocardial infarction leads to the inhibition of intestinal epithelial tight junction protein and the injury of intestinal mucosa, thereby increasing intestinal permeability.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from animal experiments, likely supported by prior research.

claim: Compared with healthy individuals, the gut microbiota of STEMI patients has higher richness and diversity.
source: It has been reported that, compared with healthy individuals, the gut microbiota of STEMI patients has higher richness and diversity (Zhou et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The number of gut microbiota species in the HPR group was significantly higher than that in the NPR group.
source: In this study, we analyzed the microbial diversity in fecal samples from the NPR and HPR groups and found that the number of gut microbiota species in the HPR group was significantly higher than that in the NPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data.

claim: The concentrations of Deinococcus and Proteus in the HPR group were significantly higher than those in the NPR group.
source: From species composition analysis, we determined that the concentrations of Deinococcus and Proteus in the HPR group were significantly higher than those in the NPR group, suggesting that the increase in intestinal harmful bacteria may affect the PA rate.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data.

claim: The increase in intestinal harmful bacteria may affect the PA rate.
source: From species composition analysis, we determined that the concentrations of Deinococcus and Proteus in the HPR group were significantly higher than those in the NPR group, suggesting that the increase in intestinal harmful bacteria may affect the PA rate.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed differences in bacterial composition.

claim: The number of Proteobacteria increased significantly in the NPR group compared with that in the HPR group.
source: In terms of species abundance, the number of Proteobacteria increased significantly in the NPR group compared with that in the HPR group.
evidence: This is supported by metagenomic analysis data.

claim: Proteobacteria adhere to a large area of gut lining, secreting a large number of enzymatic complexes, such as polysaccharides and fibrin.
source: Proteobacteria adhere to a large area of gut lining, secreting a large number of enzymatic complexes, such as polysaccharides and fibrin.
